title: Divide an Array Into Subarrays With Minimum Cost I
spaceBreakdown:
- int first, second, n: three scalar variables → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned int
approach: The first subarray must start at index 0, so its cost is always `nums[0]`. The remaining two subarrays start at two distinct indices `i < j` in `nums[1..n-1]`, contributing `nums[i] + nums[j]`. To minimize this sum, pick the two smallest values in `nums[1..n-1]` (their relative order doesn't matter since we assign the smaller index to `i` and the larger to `j`). A single linear scan tracking the smallest and second-smallest suffices.
hints: The first subarray always starts at index 0, so one of the three costs is fixed. What two quantities in the rest of the array determine the other two costs, and what constraint links their positions?
Track the smallest and second-smallest value in `nums[1..n-1]` with one linear scan. For `nums = [1,2,3,12]`, the tail `[2,3,12]` yields smallest = 2, second = 3, so the answer is `1 + 2 + 3 = 6`.

**Duplicates** - two equal smallest values in the tail.
`Input: nums = [10,1,1,5]` → `Expected: 12`
⚠️ Bug: guarding the second branch with `x > first && x < second` → second becomes 5, returns 16.

**All equal** - every element identical.
`Input: nums = [7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: 21`
⚠️ Bug: deduplicating the tail before selecting → only one distinct value found, second stays INF.

**Boundary indices** - the two smallest values sit at the last two positions.
`Input: nums = [1,5,5,3,2]` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: scanning `nums[1..n-2]` (off-by-one excluding last element) → picks 3 and 5, returns 9.

**Smallest input** - n = 3, exactly one split into three singletons.
`Input: nums = [5,4,3]` → `Expected: 12`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `second` only when `n > 3` → second stays INT_MAX, returns garbage.

followUps.q: Divide into k subarrays instead of 3 - how does the approach change?
followUps.a: The first cost is still `nums[0]`; you now need the k−1 smallest values in `nums[1..n-1]`. Maintain a max-heap of size k−1 while scanning, then sum the heap contents. TC: O(n log k), SC: O(k).

followUps.q: n up to 10^5 and k up to 10^5 - can you stay linear?
followUps.a: Use `nth_element` to partition `nums[1..n-1]` so the k−1 smallest land at the front in O(n) average, then sum them. TC: O(n), SC: O(1) in-place.

followUps.q: Cost of a subarray is its maximum element, not its first - what changes?
followUps.a: Split position now affects cost non-trivially, so use DP: `dp[i][j]` = min cost to split first i elements into j subarrays, carrying the running max of the current segment. TC: O(n²·k), SC: O(n·k).
